title: Dimension sweep and hosting paths discovery
summary: Intro discovery to evaluate embedding dimensionality, fanout and hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Customer is planning a pilot for product search rerank; they need throughput estimates and a plan for shard/fanout behavior and encryption/KMS concerns.
topics: vector DB fanout vs local rerank tradeoffs
hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) hosting criteria
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Sara (LogiQ Head of ML), Ethan (Infra), Maya (CTO)

Summary (auto): discuss embed dims and hosting path for a rerank-first product search pilot.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:07] Sara: hi, Sara here. we run product search for LogiQ, around 250m items, making recs and a straight rerank stage, trying to cut latency and costs.
[00:15] Ethan: hey, Ethan, infra lead. we'll own deployment and compliance.
[00:19] Maya: Maya, CTO. want to understand hosting paths and risk.
[00:24] Marco: Marco from Redwood, i focus on embeddings performance and throughput.
[00:29] Avery: goal for today is to understand your workload and run a dimension sweep to pick dims and hosting. starting broad: sara, what are your qps and p95 targets?
[00:38] Sara: on peak traffic we see about 150 qps of search requests, each triggers 1 fanout to vector DB retrieving top 100, then we run a rerank model over top 100 candidates. target 95th latency for user-facing is 400ms end-to-end.
[00:52] Marco: ok, and how heavy is your rerank? is it just an embed cos-sim + small transformer?
[00:58] Sara: it's a small transformer (125M) that runs on CPU for rerank currently but we want to move the expensive bits to Redwood hosting — embeddings + rerank orchestration. also trying to choose embedding dims: currently 768 but we suspect we can go down to 256 or even 128 for speed/cost.
[01:15] Avery: great. couple of clarifying things, when you say fanout of 100, is that synchronous or do you do early stopping?
[01:20] Sara: synchronous. we fetch 100 vectors, compute scores, then rerank. no early stopping today.
[01:26] Ethan: for infra, we prefer minimal external egress — ideally a VPC peering or private link into our vector DB cluster.
[01:32] Marco: Redwood offers VPC connectors for Private deployment or VPC peering for Dedicated; hosted API would go over TLS public endpoints, with encryption in transit and at rest — KMS support for Private and Dedicated.
[01:44] Maya: can you clarify the performance tradeoff for dims? like 768 to 256 — how much throughput improvement do you usually see?
[01:50] Marco: rough rule of thumb: compute scales roughly with dim, so 3x reduction from 768->256 can yield ~2.5-3x token/embedding throughput improvement on the same hardware. but retrieval fanout, vector DB indexing, and IO matter too. for rerank, if the reranker is the bottleneck, embedding dim reductions help only up to the point where rerank model saturates.
[02:08] Sara: right, and for our workload rerank model is expensive — we estimated 0.6-1.2ms per candidate on CPU right now; moving to Redwood for batched GPU rerank might help.
[02:18] Avery: have you benchmarked your vector DB on recall at lower dims? smaller dims maybe degrade recall — do you have labeled relevance sets?
[02:24] Sara: we have a small eval set (about 5k queries) with ground truth. initial tests show 256 dims only drops recall@10 by ~2.5% vs 768; 128 drops it more, like 6-8%. but those are fuzzy.
[02:39] Marco: that's a great starting point — our Optimize toolkit can run simulated cost/recall curves. we can do a dimension sweep: run 128/256/512 sample inference and measure rerank MRR and latency.
[02:50] Ethan: what about fanout cost — if we fetch 100 and then run rerank on 100 candidates, cost is high. alternatives?
[02:56] Marco: options: reduce fanout to 50 + stronger rerank, run approximate rerank (two-stage embedding cascade), or push rerank into the vector DB if it supports scoring functions. Another pattern is canonicalization: precompute dense vectors for reranker features and do a hybrid rerank where initial vector search uses small dim, then second-stage rerank uses higher-dim cached vectors for top-K.
[03:17] Sara: hybrid sounds interesting. we use Pinecone today for the index, but we were evaluating sharding and fanout costs.
[03:23] Avery: speaking of Pinecone, are you also evaluating Milvus or self-hosted Weaviate?
[03:28] Sara: yes, we chatted with Pinecone and briefly with Milvus. cost is a factor.
[03:33] Marco: (overlap) one note on hosting: Hosted Redwood is quickest to get started and we can run a pilot with limited data residency controls, Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you KMS/HSM integrations and full control.
[03:50] Ethan: are audit logs and SOC2 coverage standard on Hosted?
[03:55] Marco: Hosted is SOC2 compliant — we provide audit logs, but key management for Hosted uses our managed KMS unless you choose Dedicated with customer-managed keys or Private where you bring your KMS.
[04:06] Maya: for compliance we need customer-managed keys and all logs forwarded to our SIEM. that's a blocker for Hosted unless there are mitigation controls.
[04:14] Avery: noted. we can model a Dedicated or Private PO for that.
[04:18] Sara: back to throughput: do you have numbers for batching and KV cache hit rates for rerank? i.e., if we batch requests, what's tail latency like?
[04:25] Marco: depends on traffic patterns. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache for prefix hits (we cache embeddings and intermediate KV cache for autoregressive calls). for rerank the main lever is batching across requests — at 150 qps with 100 candidates each, if we batch to fill the GPU we can get good amortization. tail latency depends on how we set SLOs and batching windows — we can keep p95 under 300ms with dedicated GPU pools for typical rerank sizes, but p99 tails could be higher unless we reserve capacity.
[04:53] Ethan: reserved capacity pricing — can you give a ballpark?
[04:56] Avery: we'll follow up with detailed pricing but high level: Dedicated is reserved monthly for GPU pools; hosted is pay-as-you-go. we'll send a pilot pricing sheet.
[05:04] Sara: can you also run a throughput sim where we reduce dim and measure end-to-end latency with our rerank model?
[05:10] Marco: yes, we can: ask you to share a sample eval set and maybe a small binary of the rerank if allowed, or we can reproduce with an equivalent open model.
[05:19] Maya: security question again: if we go Dedicated in our cloud region, can you support VPC peering and private endpoints?
[05:25] Marco: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC if you want full on-prem parity.
[05:33] Ethan: what about cold start and cache warming for rerank?
[05:37] Marco: we recommend warming policies: pre-warm KV caches by replaying recent requests or running cold preload jobs to fill embeddings for top SKUs, and use autoscale policies for Dedicated to maintain tail latency.
[05:48] Sara: latency SLA — do you offer SLA for Dedicated?
[05:52] Avery: yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include specifics in the follow-up.
[05:59] Marco: question to you, sara — are you open to reducing fanout and moving complexity to a learned reranker so you can save on vector DB egress?
[06:06] Sara: yes, probably. we need to see the recall hit. if we can keep recall within 3% of baseline and cut costs by 30% that's a win.
[06:14] Maya: what's the shortest pilot timeline? two weeks?
[06:18] Avery: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: dimension sweep + small throughput run + security review. we can do an initial smoke test in 1 week if you provide a sample eval and credentials for a staging index.
[06:29] Ethan: credentials — we prefer to create a read-only staging index and a signed S3 sample.
[06:34] Marco: perfect. we'll need an eval set, staging index access (or a dumped sample in S3), and a brief note of your rerank model compute characteristics.
[06:43] Sara: we'll share the eval set; can you also show us a comparison sheet of hosting costs for 3 configs? hosted, dedicated (small pool), private?
[06:50] Avery: yes, we'll send a pricing matrix and an ops runbook.
[06:54] Maya: any blockers we should be aware of?
[06:57] Marco: the main blockers are: KMS/customer-managed keys for Hosted (not supported), network peering timeline for Dedicated, and data residency agreements for Private; we can surface mitigations.
[07:08] Sara: sounds good. also, do you support quantized embeddings? we were looking at 8-bit compressed vectors to reduce storage and network egress.
[07:15] Marco: we support quantized model variants for embeddings and recommend mixed-precision for exports; vector DB compatibility depends on store. quantized vectors can impact recall slightly; that's another axis for the sweep.
[07:27] Ethan: one quick thing: our finance person will need a simple TCO estimate for 12 months.
[07:31] Avery: we'll include a 12-month TCO in the follow-up.
[07:34] Marco: ok lets capture next steps.
[07:36] [crosstalk]
[07:40] Avery: recap: Redwood to run dimension sweep (128/256/512) on sample eval set, run a small throughput pilot to measure p95/p99 for 150 qps with fanout 100, provide pricing matrix for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, provide security docs (SOC2, KMS options, audit log flow), and propose dedicated sizing for reserved pool.
[07:58] Sara: thanks everyone — next call after you deliver pilot results.
[08:03] Maya: thanks.

(Transcript ends — auto timestamps approximate)
